objective: Choose useful ML experiments from task contract, observations and remaining budget; validate the selection procedure before expanding model search
mandatory_guarantees: No prohibited labels in transformations, retrieval, fitting or policy search
Only supplied Qwen as contest controlling model
No runtime downloads, installations, external training data or pretrained weights
Reproducible lineage and correct output before deadline
Separate compliance, autonomous decision quality and predictive quality
engineering_choices: No universal improvement floor, bootstrap requirement or fixed sequence
Conditional portfolio and pilot sizes; not permanent contest budgets
Recipe includes preprocessing, fit protocol, decision policy, refit and inference strategy
Existing executors reused; new model implementations must pass dependency and resource checks
completed_here: Exact input-group conflict and train/test feature overlap audit
Frozen-policy saved-model refit/prior counterfactual without new fitting
Read-only audit script and regression tests
not_completed_here: New selection protocol or runtime API changes

experiments.question: Which predeclared evaluation design predicts deployment-relevant recipe performance more reliably?
arms: Contract-aware temporal/group selector with prespecified aggregation and refit
measurement: Outer evaluation of the selection procedure
limitations: Previously inspected labels cannot provide a fresh blind final acceptance
Changing window or grouping changes the estimand; do not compare incompatible hashes

experiments.question: Does a faithful strong neural baseline with numeric embeddings add useful errors beyond trees?
arms: Same backbone with fit-only numeric embeddings
measurement: CPU wall time and peak memory
constraints: Train from scratch with allowed PyTorch
Do not label simplified variants as full author reproductions
experiments.pilot: Two or three recipes across two task-appropriate parts after a bounded resource pilot; actual counts chosen from budget

experiments.question: Does learned local similarity improve predictions or provide complementary errors?
arms: ModernNCA with declared preprocessing and neighbor sampling
measurement: Training and complete test inference cost
constraints: Chunking changes memory, not pair count
Top-k inference is a separate approximation
experiments.pilot: One bounded fit plus full-size inference pilot before allocating a comparison series

experiments.question: Does an OOF combiner beat a simple stable blend under the actual transfer setting?
constraints: Evaluation labels excluded from all meta-training and weight tuning
Shared-fit calibration halves are not an OOF matrix

experiments.question: Does one feature representation or feature-only error gate address a confirmed error region?
arms: One prespecified feature-group transformation or fitted feature-only gate
constraints: No true query tail/target used for routing
Retain and report negative prior feature experiments
measurement: Raw-scale RMSE or declared classification metric
experiments.pilot: One hypothesis per comparison; tail mixture requires one gate and two regressors

experiments.question: Is a specific shift assumption sufficiently plausible to test bounded correction?
entry_conditions: Overlap or identifiable class confusion structure
constraints: Domain separability does not prove conditional invariance

experiments.question: Can a local learned-kernel prototype be implemented and evaluated inside the fixed CPU dependency budget?
measurement: Pilot fit and complete inference time
experiments.pilot: Small resource prototype before any full-series allocation

acceptance_axes.compliance: Offline boundary and complete runtime checks; research alone insufficient
acceptance_axes.autonomy: Supplied-Qwen traces, evidence-linked next decisions and justified stopping; not measured by reference fits
acceptance_axes.prediction: Same task/evaluation design and resources; old inspected controls descriptive; hidden-test quality unknown

stop_conditions: Repeated negative outcomes without a materially different question
